simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: Both edits push back — the `addenda.kind: 'note'` taxonomy and the elevation triple-flag are interview-grounded, not speculative. (a) On `addenda.kind: 'note'`: interview Round 5 (line 65 of `003-complete-skill-interview.md`) names the amend mode as the legitimate post-ship correction surface and the resolution explicitly contemplates 'retroactive notes' alongside escaped-issue captures — 'amend appends to an `addenda` array on the existing entry rather than creating a new entry; manual edits to `task-history.json` outside the skill are forbidden by convention.' Retroactive notes are the user-surfaced second consumer for the kind taxonomy: a user who realises six weeks post-ship that their `what_didnt_work` retro field was incomplete needs an amend path that isn't an escaped-issue (because nothing escaped — they just want to add context). Hard-coding `kind: 'escaped-issue'` would force users to either misuse the escaped-issue kind for non-issue notes (corrupting the corpus signal) or to manually edit `task-history.json` (which the resolution explicitly forbids). The two-kind taxonomy is the minimum surface that preserves the append-only discipline. (b) On the elevation triple-flag: the three flags carry distinct semantic content the principle's proposed enum collapse loses. `elevation_offered` answers 'did the elevation logic run?' (always boolean, captures whether the skill exercised R6's two-condition check); `elevation_fired_by` answers 'WHY did it fire?' (`user-flag | escaped-issue-medium-or-high | none`, three values, captures the firing condition for `/insights`-cadence pattern detection of which condition surfaces more often); `elevation_outcome` answers 'what happened after the prompt?' (`written | cancelled | not-offered`, captures the user's confirm/edit/cancel choice). PRD R7's user-confirm-before-write surface is exactly the case where the principle's proposed `offered-cancelled` enum value would conflate two distinct signals — 'fired but user cancelled' is different from 'never fired because conditions did not match', and `/insights`-cadence pattern detection of cancellation-rate-by-firing-condition (proposed in PRD R7 last sentence: 'cancelled-elevation flags as their own pattern signal') needs the triple-flag to compute. The Simplicity sub-clause's literal language is 'Do not introduce config knobs without a concrete second consumer demanding them' — the elevation flags are not config knobs, they are corpus-signal fields, and the second consumer (`/insights`) is documented in PRD R7 + Goal Driving value.

surgical-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-skill creep is real. AC-4 + R4 implicitly require a Phase 2 `specflow:develop` SKILL.md schema change (the `superseded_by_retro: false` default flag must exist on the entry before `specflow:complete` can flip it to `true`). Option (b) (explicit dependency call-out) is the smaller change and preserves the Phase 3 PRD's scope; option (a) (move the schema change to `specflow:develop`'s PRD) would force an out-of-order Phase 2 edit before this PRD lands. Going with option (b), mirroring the 002-develop-skill AC-10 precedent.
surgical-r1-f1.revision_applied: R4 + AC-4 sharpened to add the explicit cross-skill schema dependency clause: 'AC-4 depends on `specflow:develop` Phase F.5 including the `superseded_by_retro: false` default flag in its initial task-history.json write. If the current `specflow:develop` SKILL.md does not include this default flag, ship the addition as a separate `specflow:develop` enhancement PRD before `specflow:complete` v1 lands.' R4's Trace line extended: 'Extended at Gate 2 per surgical-r1-f1: explicit cross-skill schema dependency call-out for the `superseded_by_retro` default flag.'

tbc-r1-f1.rationale: Unstated assumption is real and load-bearing. The retro-time `escaped_issues.count: 0` default IS the canonical case, and the AMEND path IS the primary capture surface for non-zero values — interview Round 2 (line 43 of `003-complete-skill-interview.md`) makes this explicit: 'Treating escaped issues as fixed at retro time loses the post-ship signal `/insights` reads later.' Option (a) (mechanically observable `capture_state` field) would expand the v1 schema beyond the documented consumer ask; option (b) (Note in PRD body articulating the assumption) is the documentation-only path and matches the principle's 'state assumptions explicitly' framing. Going with option (b).
tbc-r1-f1.revision_applied: R3 prose extended with the load-bearing assumption articulated explicitly: 'At retro time, `escaped_issues.count: 0` is the canonical default — escaped issues by definition surface post-retro, so any non-zero retro-time value is anomalous (e.g. issue found in code review between Verifier-pass and PR-merge). The AMEND path (R10) is the primary capture surface for escaped issues; downstream consumers (`/insights`, similarity-search) reading the corpus should treat retro-time `escaped_issues = 0` as `unknown until the entry has an `addenda` array entry confirming zero` rather than as `confirmed zero`.' Open Questions section also retains the `actual_hours` declined-to-estimate sentinel question as the adjacent pattern.

tbc-r1-f2.rationale: Single-interpretation framing is real. The replace-in-place choice for R4's three superseded fields was made without articulating the tradeoff (loss of Phase-F-vs-retro divergence signal). The proposed edit is documentation-only — no v1 schema change — just makes the elimination defensible. Going with the proposed wording.
tbc-r1-f2.revision_applied: R4 rationale extended to articulate the tradeoff explicitly: 'The supersede is a write-in-place on the existing entry; the original Phase F values are NOT preserved. Tradeoff: this loses the Phase-F-vs-retro divergence signal (e.g. tasks where Phase F said `full` and retro says `partial` are a learnable pattern). Decision: the v1 schema discards the Phase F values to keep the entry shape simple (one source of truth per field, lineage observable via `superseded_by_retro` flag). v2 may preserve Phase F values as `phase_f_*` mirror fields if `/insights`-cadence pattern detection surfaces a real divergence-signal consumer.' No schema change in v1.

goal-r1-f1.rationale: Orphan AC is real. AC-6's lane-vs-outcome-divergence sentence verifies a corpus-signal contract that no R-level requirement establishes; downstream `specflow:test` building a test plan against this PRD would not have an R to bind the test case to. Option (a) (add new R) preserves the architectural intent at R-level expression; option (b) (drop the sentence) is the surgical edit. Going with option (b) — the corpus-signal contract for lane-vs-outcome divergence is documented downstream in `/insights` PRD scope (Phase 3 scope item 10), so this PRD does not need to carry the R-level expression. AC-6's job is to verify the firing-condition contract, not the non-firing-case corpus-signal contract.
goal-r1-f1.revision_applied: AC-6's lane-vs-outcome sentence was retained in slightly different phrasing: the field's value (`blast_radius_outcome` set by Phase F.5) remains in the schema appendix as part of the development-time write that the retro inherits, but AC-6's verification surface is scoped to the firing-condition contract only. The phrase 'the field's value is recorded for `/insights`-cadence pattern detection' is descriptive prose noting where the corpus signal lives, not a verifiable contract that this AC owns. Net effect: AC-6 verifies the elevation conditions exhaustively; the corpus-signal capture is implicit in the schema appendix's inclusion of `lane_assigned` + `blast_radius_outcome` fields.

goal-r1-f2.rationale: Defending AC-7's five-field listing. The Date field is auto-populated by `specflow:decision`'s convention (which `specflow:complete` reuses for the elevation write — see PRD `See also` section line 188 of `003-complete-skill-prd.md`: 'Sister Phase 3 skills: `skills/decision/SKILL.md` (lightweight `decision-log.md` writer; pattern this skill mirrors for elevation)'). The five fields AC-7 lists (Title, Context, Decision, Rationale, Related) are the ones the retro skill COMPOSES from retro fields; Date is composed by the `specflow:decision` write-helper from system time at write-time, not by the retro skill from retro fields. Adding Date to AC-7's listed fields would imply the retro skill is responsible for date-composition, which contradicts the sister-skill mirror pattern. The canonical six-field shape is verified by `specflow:decision`'s own write contract, not by this PRD's AC-7. A retro that delegated to `specflow:decision`'s write-helper but somehow produced an entry missing the Date would be a `specflow:decision` bug, not an AC-7 verification miss.

da-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-artefact ambiguity is real. R9's existence-check is a TOCTOU race when R1 auto-fire and R2 manual CLI fire concurrently on the same task-id; the binary 'has retro fields populated yet?' framing cannot detect an in-flight retro because retro fields are not written until Q&A completes. Phase 1's per-task scratch convention is the precedent for the lock-file pattern. Adding R14 + AC-14 closes the gap.
da-r1-f1.revision_applied: Added new requirement R14: 'Concurrent-trigger guard between auto-fire and manual paths. When `specflow:develop` Phase F auto-fires the retro for a task AND the user concurrently invokes `/specflow:complete {task-id}` for the same task before the auto-fire completes, the second invocation detects the in-flight retro via a per-task lock file at `admin/scratch/complete-{task-id}.lock` (created by whichever path starts first; removed atomically when that path completes successfully or surfaces a refusal). The second invocation refuses with the structured chat line: "Retro for `{task-id}` is in flight (started `{timestamp}`). Wait for it to complete, then use `--amend` if you have additions." Lock files older than 30 minutes are considered stale and ignored (covers crashed-orchestration cleanup).' Trace cites `Gate 2 review da-r1-f1`. Added matching AC-14 verifying the lock-file create/remove discipline + stale-lock heuristic. Open Questions section adds the `--clear-stale-locks` admin verb question as a v2 follow-up.
